timeline.body:
Executable Starlark rules can use the `run_under_env` parameter of `RunEnvironmentInfo` to define an environment variable with the value of `--run_under` when it's set. This is useful in cases where executable targets execute some sort of process-wrapper which either sub-processes or execs into the expected process. Before, `--run_under` would happen on the process wrapper which made debuggers and profiling tools harder to use as the process they were attached to was not the process users cared about. 

After this change, by having an executable Starlark rule return `RunEnvironmentInfo(run_under_env = "RUN_UNDER_VALUE")`, `run` or `test` invocations which pass `--run_under='strace -c'` will cause the executable to have `RUN_UNDER_VALUE='strace -c'` set in it's environment.

RELNOTES: Executable Starlark rules can use the `run_under_env` parameter of `RunEnvironmentInfo` to define an environment variable with the value of `--run_under` when it's set. This allows Starlark rule authors to control how this value is used.

closes https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/16232

Some open questions for this draft:
- How are integration tests written for Bazel?
- Should the value set to `run_under_env` include the shell executable?

```suggestion
   * Returns the name of the environment variable to pass the "run_under" value to.
```

```suggestion
              runUnderEnv == Starlark.NONE ? null : (String) runUnderEnv,
```

More likely to catch type issues.
You can set IntelliJ up for formatting according to the Google Java Style Guide with https://github.com/google/styleguide/blob/gh-pages/intellij-java-google-style.xml.

You can use [`google-java-format`](https://github.com/google/google-java-format) and run it from VSC [like this](https://stackoverflow.com/a/59718005/297261).

Thanks! Though after formatting the code it seems there's quite a lot that's unformatted. It might be helpful to contributors to have some maintainer run the formatter on all files. Additionally, I noticed `bazel build //...` does not work in the repo, which I found odd.

A workaround for the formatting problem is to only format changed lines with [this tool](https://github.com/google/google-java-format/blob/master/scripts/google-java-format-diff.py). A Bazel-wide reformat would require all PRs to go through relatively painful rebases, which may be why it hasn't been done yet.

I think that there was an issue about making `bazel build //...` pass, but I can't find it right now. `bazel test //...` would require fetching a hermetic Android NDK, which AFAIK isn't possible due to the license acceptance step. I usually just check that `bazel build //src:bazel-dev` completes and then fix test build breakages reported by CI.

> * How are integration tests written for Bazel?

Given that the existing `RunEnvironmentInfo` tests are in https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/b5db37924fc204eff4ed6ebbccba18da972bf538/src/test/shell/bazel/bazel_rules_test.sh#L670, you should probably add shell tests there. 

> * Should the value set to run_under_env include the shell executable?

That is a good question I don't have a good answer to - I yet have to use `--run_under` in a non-trivial way. Do Starlark rules have access to the shell toolchain?

> Do Starlark rules have access to the shell toolchain?

I don't think so. I'm not aware of `shell_toolchain` being something that exists. I think if I could get an integration test it might lead to an answer here.
@fmeum I noticed you did not have a change like like this for `arugments` in your PR. Was that intentional? Is this needed?

reply.body:
That was intentional: Adding such a method/struct field would give Starlark rules access to this information in the provider. I wasn't sure whether `arguments` is something that other rules should be able to inspect, so I decided not to expose it for now.

Do you see a reason for depending rules to access the value of `run_under_env`? If there is no clear use case, it may be better not to expose it for now. API creep is real and incompatible changes removing functionality are painful.

Note that depending rules can always just forward the provider unchanged, so not exposing this doesn't prevent e.g. transition wrappers.

reply.body: Sure, though in general I would expect all default values for rules to use `Label(...)` since it offers more consistent results across repository boundaries. It's not strictly needed for this test but would be a better thing for other devs to pattern match.
I _think_ that's not true: `default = "..."` and `default = Label("...")` should be exactly equivalent. Using `Label` is relevant in macros, but shouldn't be in rule definitions.

reply.body: I wanted to use `pkg/run_under.(sh|bat)` directly instead of needing to render the same content into a starlark constant to be written in this rule. This is one of the few actions that let me copy files.
I replaced it with `ct.actions.symlink` which I was originally nervous about using because of windows but that seems to work 😄
It will do a copy if symlinks aren't enabled. Keep calm and symlink on 🙂

+function test_starlark_rule_with_run_under_env() {

+EOF
+
+  # On Windows this file needs to be acceptable by CreateProcessW(), rather
+  # than a Bourne script.
+  if "$is_windows"; then
+    local run_under_script="pkg/run_under.bat"
+    echo 'exports_files(["run_under.bat"])' >> pkg/BUILD
+    cat >pkg/run_under.bat <<'EOF'
+@ECHO OFF
+if not defined RUN_UNDER_VALUE (
+  echo --run_under script was unexpectedly executed
+)
+if "%1%"=="--exit_code" (
+  exit /B %2%
+)
+exit /B 101
+EOF
+    cat >pkg/rules.bzl <<'EOF'
+_SCRIPT_EXT = ".bat"
+_SCRIPT_CONTENT = """
+@ECHO OFF
+if not defined RUN_UNDER_VALUE (
+  echo run_under_env value is not set
+  exit /B 1
+)
+set _EXPECTED_EXIT_CODE=101
+if not "%RUN_UNDER_VALUE:--exit_code=%"=="%RUN_UNDER_VALUE%" (
+  set _EXPECTED_EXIT_CODE=202
+)
+start /b /wait bash.exe -c "%RUN_UNDER_VALUE%"
+if %ERRORLEVEL% NEQ %_EXPECTED_EXIT_CODE% (
+  echo Failed to execute run_under_env value
+  exit /B 1
+)
+exit /B 0
+"""
+EOF
+  else
+  local run_under_script="pkg/run_under.sh"
+  echo 'exports_files(["run_under.sh"])' >> pkg/BUILD
+    cat >pkg/run_under.sh <<'EOF'
+#!/bin/bash
+if [[ -z "${RUN_UNDER_VALUE}" ]]; then
+  echo --run_under script was unexpectedly executed
+fi
+if [[ "${1:-}" == "--exit_code" ]]; then
+  exit $2
+fi
+exit 101
+EOF
+    chmod +x pkg/run_under.sh
+    cat >pkg/rules.bzl <<'EOF'
+_SCRIPT_EXT = ".sh"
+_SCRIPT_CONTENT = """#!/bin/bash
+if [[ -z "${RUN_UNDER_VALUE:-}" ]]; then
+  echo "run_under_env value is not set"
+  exit 1
+fi
+export _EXPECTED_EXIT_CODE=101
+if [[ "${RUN_UNDER_VALUE}" == *"--exit_code"* ]]; then
+  export _EXPECTED_EXIT_CODE=202
+fi
+bash -c "${RUN_UNDER_VALUE}"
+if [[ $? != ${_EXPECTED_EXIT_CODE} ]]; then
+  echo "Failed to execute run_under_env value"
+  exit 1
+fi
+exit 0
+"""
+EOF
+  fi
+
+  cat >>pkg/rules.bzl <<'EOF'
+def _my_executable_impl(ctx):
+    executable_sh = ctx.actions.declare_file(ctx.attr.name + _SCRIPT_EXT)

+        output = executable_sh,
+        content = _SCRIPT_CONTENT,
+        is_executable = True,
+    )
+    return [
+        DefaultInfo(

+        ),
+        RunEnvironmentInfo(
+            run_under_env = "RUN_UNDER_VALUE",
+        ),
+    ]
+
+my_executable = rule(

+    attrs = {},
+    executable = True,
+)
+
+my_test = rule(

+    attrs = {},
+    test = True,
+)
+
+def _my_wrapper_impl(ctx):
+    executable_sh = ctx.actions.declare_file(ctx.attr.name + _SCRIPT_EXT)

+

+    || fail "Test binary with target should have exit code 0"
+
+  # Test --run_under as a custom command
+  bazel run //pkg:my_executable --run_under="$(pwd)/${run_under_script}" >$TEST_log 2>&1 \
+    || fail "Run binary with command should have exit code 0"
+
+  # Test --run_under as a custom command with args
+  bazel run //pkg:my_executable --run_under="$(pwd)/${run_under_script} --exit_code 202" >$TEST_log 2>&1 \
+    || fail "Run binary with command should have exit code 0"
+
+  # Test --run_under as a target
+  bazel run //pkg:my_executable --run_under=//pkg:my_wrapper >$TEST_log 2>&1 \
+    || fail "Run binary with target should have exit code 0"
